h1:
Phayao–Chiang Rai
A Road Trip Across Thailand's Far North
intro: Phayao and Chiang Rai sit right next to each other, an easy hour and a half of driving apart, which makes them a natural pair for one trip. Start in Phayao for slow lakeside days, head up Phu Langka for the sea of fog, then cross into Chiang Rai to see Wat Rong Khun, drive up Doi Tung, and finish at the Golden Triangle, the northernmost tip of Thailand. We've laid it out as 3 days and 2 nights with enough room to actually stop and enjoy each place, not rush yourself ragged.

blocks.html: A Phayao–Chiang Rai trip suits anyone who wants the quiet of a smaller province and the variety of a bigger one in a single run. Phayao gives you the lakeside mood, quiet cafés and mountains the crowds haven't fully found yet. Chiang Rai brings art temples, tea plantations and Mekong-side viewpoints at the very top of the country. The two provinces are only about 90 kilometres apart along Highway 1 (Phahonyothin), roughly an hour and a half of driving on good roads, with plenty of spots to break up the journey.

The setup that works best is driving yourself, because Phu Langka, Doi Tung and the Golden Triangle all sit well outside the towns and public transport barely reaches them. Coming from Bangkok, flying into Chiang Rai and renting a car saves the most time. You can also fly into Chiang Mai and drive about 3 hours on to Phayao. If you're driving straight up from Bangkok, count on around 10–11 hours, so we'd suggest an overnight stop along the way.

items: Phayao → Chiang Rai — Highway 1, about 90 km, roughly 1 hr 30 min
Phayao town → Phu Langka (Pong district) — about 80 km; the final climb up the mountain is narrow and steep, so use a car in good shape
Chiang Rai town → Doi Tung — about 60 km of winding mountain road, around 1 hr 15 min
Doi Tung → Golden Triangle (Chiang Saen district) — about 40 km, and you can pass through Mae Sai

blocks.title: Plan Your Direction Smartly
blocks.html: Do Phayao first, then flow up into Chiang Rai so you never have to double back. Phu Langka is on the eastern side of Phayao, while Doi Tung and the Golden Triangle are at the far north, so it all lines up as one continuous route with no backtracking.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Lakeside Phayao + Up to Phu Langka

items.activity: Pay respects to Phra Chao Ton Luang at Wat Si Khom Kham
items.note: The largest principal Buddha image in Lanna, right by Kwan Phayao lake. It opens early, before the crowds arrive

items.activity: Stroll along Kwan Phayao and find a café by the water
items.note: Kwan Phayao is the largest freshwater lake in northern Thailand, with several viewpoints and lakeside coffee shops

items.activity: Take a boat to Wat Tilok Aram, the temple in the middle of the lake
items.note: The temple sits out in the middle of the lake; you board a boat from the pier and the fare is only a few dozen baht per person

items.activity: Lunch in town — khanom jeen nam ngiao or khao soi
items.note: Northern food in Phayao costs less than in the bigger cities, around 40–60 THB a plate

items.activity: Drive up to Pong district, heading for Phu Langka
items.note: About 80 km, with the last stretch climbing the mountain. Aim to reach your lodging before dark since there are no street lights

items.activity: Check in on Phu Langka and walk out to the Pha Chang Noi viewpoint
items.note: It's cool here year-round, so pack a jacket if you're coming in winter

items.activity: Watch the sunset, then have dinner at your lodging
items.note: Dining options up on the mountain are limited, so it's easier to arrange meals with your accommodation in advance

blocks.title: About Lodging on Phu Langka
blocks.html: Accommodation on Phu Langka is limited and fills up very fast in the cool season (Nov–Jan). If you're going then, book several weeks ahead. If you can't get a room in time, stay in Phayao town and drive up before dawn to catch the fog instead — but you'll need to be up by 4 or 5 in the morning.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Morning Sea of Fog, Then Over to Chiang Rai

items.activity: Wake up for the sea of fog at the Phu Langka viewpoint
items.note: Pre-dawn until around 7am is the prime window for the fog. If the sky is clear, you'll see layered ridges floating above the mist

items.activity: Coffee at Magic Mountain café on the cliff edge
items.note: Phu Langka's well-known café — sit with the mountain view and a warm coffee before heading down

items.activity: Pack up, head down the mountain and on to Chiang Rai
items.note: Drive down to Highway 1 and continue north — roughly 130–150 km total depending on your starting point

items.activity: Reach Chiang Rai, eat before visiting Wat Rong Khun
items.note: There are plenty of restaurants near Wat Rong Khun; keep lunch light before walking the temple

items.activity: Visit Wat Rong Khun (the White Temple)
items.note: The work of artist Chalermchai Kositpipat. Entry for Thai visitors is 100 THB; dress modestly, and it gets crowded in the afternoon

items.activity: On to Wat Rong Suea Ten (the Blue Temple)
items.note: A blue temple trimmed in gold, free to enter, on the town side — about 20 minutes' drive from Wat Rong Khun

items.activity: Check in around town and walk the Chiang Rai Night Bazaar
items.note: It has food courts and souvenirs, an easy place to grab dinner

blocks.text: Day 3 — Doi Tung, Tea Plantations and a Far-North Finish

items.activity: Leave town heading for Doi Tung
items.note: The mountain road winds a lot and takes around 1 hr 15 min — drive slowly and watch for oncoming cars

items.activity: Visit Mae Fah Luang Garden and the Doi Tung Royal Villa
items.note: Cool-climate flower gardens rotate through the year, with separate entry fees by zone, and the weather is pleasantly cool

items.activity: Stop at Choui Fong Tea plantation and photograph the green tea fields
items.note: Terraced tea fields with wide views, plus a café and green tea cake — a good spot for a late-morning break

items.activity: Drive up to Chiang Saen district to the Golden Triangle
items.note: Where the Mekong meets the Ruak River, with Thailand, Myanmar and Laos all in one frame

items.activity: Pay respects to Phra Phuttha Nawa Lan Tue and walk along the Mekong
items.note: There's a riverside terrace overlooking the Mekong and the Golden Triangle archway to photograph

items.activity: Stop at Mae Sai, the northernmost point of Siam
items.note: If you still have energy, go up the skywalk at Wat Phra That Doi Wao, or photograph the northernmost-point sign before heading back

blocks.text: Adjust the Plan to the Time You Have

items.name: Only 2 days
items.blurb: Skip Phu Langka, spend half a day in Phayao town, then cross to Chiang Rai and cover Wat Rong Khun, Doi Tung and the Golden Triangle on the second day.

items.name: 4 days or more
items.blurb: Add Un Phu Sang Waterfall in Phayao plus Phu Chi Fa and Doi Pha Tang on the Chiang Rai side for another sea-of-fog spot.

items.name: Temple-focused
items.blurb: Hit Wat Si Khom Kham, Wat Tilok Aram, Wat Rong Khun, Wat Rong Suea Ten and Wat Huay Pla Kang in Chiang Rai.

blocks.text: When to Go and What to Pack

items: Nov–Feb — the season with the thickest fog and coolest weather, ideal for Phu Langka and Doi Tung. But mountain lodging fills up fast, so book ahead
Mar–May — hot, and there can be haze from agricultural burning, so visibility on the mountains may be poor. Check the air-quality readings before you go
Jun–Oct — the rainy season; everything is green and the waterfalls look great, but the mountain roads get slippery, so use a capable vehicle and drive carefully
What to bring — a jacket (the mountains are cool year-round), a shawl for visiting temples, comfortable walking shoes, and cash for entry fees and boat fares

blocks.title: Fuel and Rest Stops
blocks.html: Between Pong district and the road up the mountain, fuel stations are far apart, so always fill up before climbing. The same goes for the Doi Tung–Chiang Saen stretch, where convenience stores are harder to find than in town.

faq.q: Is it worth visiting Phayao and Chiang Rai in one trip?
faq.a: Yes. The two provinces are right next to each other, only about an hour and a half of driving apart on Highway 1, so you can run them as a single route heading north with no backtracking. It works well as a 3-day, 2-night trip.

faq.q: How far is Phayao from Chiang Rai, and how long does it take?
faq.a: It's about 90 kilometres and roughly 1 hour 30 minutes of driving along Highway 1. The road is in good condition and you can easily stop at points along the way.

faq.q: Do I need to drive myself, or is there public transport?
faq.a: Driving yourself is by far the easiest, because Phu Langka, Doi Tung and the Golden Triangle all sit outside the towns and public transport barely reaches them. If you'd rather not drive, hire a car with a driver or take day tours in segments.

faq.q: When is the best time to see the sea of fog at Phu Langka?
faq.a: November to February has the thickest fog and the coolest weather. The fog shows best from pre-dawn until around 7am, and if the sky is clear you'll clearly see layered ridges floating above the mist.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Wat Rong Khun and Wat Rong Suea Ten?
faq.a: Wat Rong Khun charges Thai visitors around 100 THB, while Wat Rong Suea Ten is free to enter. Dress modestly at both, as they are places of worship.
